summary.title: How to Study: A Brief Guide
summary.one_liner: A practical, evidence-informed guide to studying by taking complete notes, rewriting them, reading slowly and actively, and using repeated self-testing rather than passive re-reading.
takeaways: Rewrite and reorganize class notes at home; copying them is itself a study method.
Read slowly and actively, asking after each sentence whether you understand, and escalate unclear points to peers, TAs, or the instructor.
Passive re-reading gives an illusion of competence; repeated self-testing and the read-recite-review method work better.
Start exam preparation about a week early, avoid cramming, and build a day-by-day schedule across multiple exams.
The author cites research (e.g., Pashler et al. 2009) finding no evidence that matching instruction to learning styles helps.
summary.summary: This is a long study guide by William Rapaport (Philosophy and Cognitive Science, University at Buffalo), last updated February 2024. It covers time management, note-taking in class and rewriting notes at home, studying hard subjects first in a quiet place, active and slow reading (with a pseudocode-style procedure), homework, exam preparation and exam-taking, and writing research essays. The author draws on personal experience and cites psychology research, such as studies on retrieval practice and on the lack of evidence for learning styles. It also includes a references list and links to further study resources.
